evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches into details without framing time/scope or getting explicit yes: 'Looks like we are moving from 10510 west Eliana trace drive...' immediately after contact confirmation.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after significant probing has started: 'Besides pricing, do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call?' — but this comes after contact info is already being collected, not before.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised concerns (couch size, TVs, patio furniture) but rep did not probe deeper; moved through a checklist instead. N/A because no real *concerns about the move itself* were raised — only inventory details.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection summary offered. N/A for same reason — no stated concerns to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Apartment, unit 382, 750 sq ft, 1 bedroom, 3rd floor, elevator type confirmed, walking distance (100-150 ft), patio furniture noted, destination apartment/unit confirmed, arrival parking (20 ft). Seven items all covered.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: 'A typical box count for a move the size is about fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you feel like you fall within that range?' — Customer answered they have crates already loaded.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: 'I would estimate that your move would take between three and four hours. So for the three, I would look to budget $682 and then for the four hours $886' — anchored to typical range for this size; personalized to the two TVs and couch as special considerations.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full disclosure: '$204 [hourly rate]... includes everything, fuel and truck the taxes and insurance. All wrap pads and bands... no hidden fees of any sort, no credit card fees, no Sterba fees... no deposit required... no changes or fees for changing the date or canceling the move.' Two and a half hour minimum, fifteen minute increments mentioned. $70 trip fee disclosed upfront.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moved directly to time-window options after pricing: 'I do have two slots for the size of your move...' with no check for customer agreement on the price itself.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full coverage: 'We do have our on time guarantee we do value your time. So, we can't make it in a time window that we arrange. We immediately start discounting money of your final bill... the time starts as soon as we get on site open that contract...'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full: 'We have our no worries, damage coverage. Which is our free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages. And that's on top of the 60¢ state mandated coverage...' — no deductible, no fine print framing, built into rate.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No loop-closing question asked after the two promises. No 'does that put those to rest?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway: 'Do you have any other questions for me while you have me?' — empty, automatic no-answer phrasing, not genuine.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep ends with: 'Let me email all this over to you and then you can reply to the email to get on our schedule or you can just give us a call back...' — no ask for the business, only a soft handoff to email/callback.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: 'There are also no changes or fees for changing the date or canceling the move' — implies rate lock implicitly, but not explicitly stated as a rate-lock guarantee.

top_strength: Brianne gathered comprehensive logistics details systematically and delivered both of the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) with full transparency and clarity.
coaching_note: Open with the quid pro quo framing and a genuine wait for yes before diving into discovery; ask for the business explicitly at the close rather than defaulting to email/callback; and ask 'Does that feel fair?' after pricing before moving to next steps.
